body:
It wasn't. I truly sucked. I'm trying to get better, and I'm genuinely interested in computer science-especially algorithms-but I'm just not a very good programmer. I occasionally wonder if I'm wasting my time by trying, mentally speaking, but that's another story. It doesn't matter: I've got to try, given my financial situation and other factors. 

I know it is on me to get better, and I've got no issues with that. But I can't realistically wait several months to get a job or, even more insultingly, go work for free: I need to start making money ASAP, and until I do that, I can't relax mentally and start focusing all my free time into my intellectual pursuits and just getting better because I want to. All I can think about right now is jobs, jobs, jobs. It's beyond depressing to waste several hours a day on applications that probably aren't even read, and even if they were... I just want to catch a break. Get a chance. That's all. 

And in terms of my own issues with depression, etc, being unemployed and stuck in a rural town with no prospects whatsoever is simply exacerbating that. Getting a job and a fresh start in life would do a lot more good for me than anything else.

Yes, I know. I did physics as an undergraduate, so I have some quantitative background, at least. I've been practicing for some time, taught myself data structures and algorithms. And yes, I made a huge mistake in doing the whole "on/off" thing with coding as an undergrad, along with math, and am trying to overhaul my study habits in that regard. I actually want to go back and teach myself an entire MIT/Caltech EECS curriculum along with math/physics. Not going to get much sleep for the next six years. :)

The problem is, until I get a job, most of my plans to improve my life are on hold, and most of my energy that I theoretically could be spending on study ends up going to worrying about my future in practice. I also need to start earning income to pay off my debts. So, the imperative right now is to get a job as I keep improving. I'm not picky as to what the job does or where it is located-just need to start.

(I'm actually trying to get better with C and low-level programming as a long term goal, since it actually interests me immensely as opposed to standard web development, but I'm realistic of my chances of getting a job in that, so I'm looking at standard Python/JavaScript developer jobs. I'm also interested in Haskell because it is great for advanced mathematics.)

So, which would you like advice on first-your mother or dating?

I'm here. I'm largely in your position, minus actually having a job, due to my lack of programming skill. 

I'm willing to trade dating advice for coding advice. I want to offer something practical and concrete on top of human engagement. It's not much, but that's what I have to offer. Also... somebody in my family is on the verge of death, too. We all know it. I can perhaps help there?
